Disease of the urethra, included in the renal axis.

Primary vertebral and metaphyseal bone dysplasia with contractures; frequency of associated intellectual disability or respiratory impairment is unclear.

Primary neoplasm arising in cardiac lining, myocardium or pericardium.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; extracolonic cancers are separate disease risks, not additional existing organ damage.
Capillary and arteriovenous malformations define vascular disease; intracranial vascular malformation is very rare and does not establish brain injury.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing the Brugada phenotype; no additional organ damage established.
Motor neuron disorder; defining lower-limb denervation causes muscle atrophy and weakness in most patients.
Inherited central movement disorder with dystonia in 19/19; muscular contractions do not establish a separate muscle disease.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder defined by skeletal myopathy; renal insufficiency occurs in 5/28 and does not meet the involvement threshold.
MELAS is defined by mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes; no additional organ reaches a supported threshold here.
Bacterial infection of lung parenchyma.
Cutis laxa, developmental impairment and corneal disease define syndrome; skeletal deformities and joint laxity occur in 80-99%; dental abnormalities omitted by cap.
Umbrella concept defined by disease of the lung.
Arenaviral hemorrhagic fever defined by infection and disordered hemostasis; vomiting, petechiae and possible coma do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited abnormality of cutaneous dermatoglyphic ridge patterns.
Mitochondrial disorder defined by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and muscular hypotonia; myopathy is frequent (30-79%).
Limb bone dysplasia with shortening, fusion and dislocations; definition explicitly states normal intelligence despite conflicting HPO cognitive annotation.
Inherited cerebral white-matter disease with episodic memory impairment.
Gonadal failure and hypogonadism define endocrine involvement; urethral malformations, including hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies, are frequent (30-79%).
Defined by recurrent metabolic crises and encephalomyopathic regression; lactic acidosis, weakness and abnormal muscle fibers support metabolic and muscle disease.
